skill.name: jira-workflow
skill.description: Orchestrate Jira story creation, approval, status transitions, and implementation updates for agile delivery teams.
skill.summary: Guide Jira stories from proposal through approval, workflow transitions, and completion updates.

security_audit.summary: Most backtick and key detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline API paths, and JavaScript template literals. I confirmed expected Jira REST network calls and environment-based credential handling, including a contextual risk where Basic auth is sent to an unvalidated base URL. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated Jira destination for authenticated requests
remediation.suggestion: Validate JIRA_BASE_URL against an approved Atlassian tenant before building the Authorization header or making fetch calls.

remediation.issue: Jira API token handling in examples
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege token scopes, secure storage, rotation, and a rule that tokens must never be logged.

remediation.issue: Implementation metadata can be posted externally
remediation.suggestion: Ask before posting files, commits, or notes to Jira, and redact sensitive paths or internal details.

remediation.issue: Executable script examples are referenced but not included in the scanned package
remediation.suggestion: Remove script-running examples or include reviewed scripts with dry-run and confirmation safeguards.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Jira Base URL Can Receive Basic Auth
semantic_findings.description: The examples build Basic authentication from Jira credentials, then use JIRA_BASE_URL directly for REST calls. If that value points outside the intended Atlassian tenant, credentials and issue data can be sent to an untrusted host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token is read from process.env and encoded into the Authorization header. The fetch destination is built from an environment-provided base URL with no allowlist or hostname validation.

semantic_findings.title: Implementation Metadata Posted to Jira Comments
semantic_findings.description: The workflow posts modified files, commits, and notes to Jira comments. This is useful synchronization, but it can disclose repository metadata to an external Jira tenant.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow passes files, commits, and notes into addImplementationDetails, which posts to Jira. The risk depends on tenant trust and the sensitivity of those details.

content.value_statement: Coordinating Jira stories, approvals, and status changes can slow delivery. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable Jira workflow.
actual_capabilities: Builds SAFe-style Jira story proposals with acceptance criteria and definitions of done.
Requires user approval before creating Jira stories from a proposal.
Shows how to create Jira stories and subtasks through REST API calls.
Guides transitions through To Do, Progressing, In Review, Out Review, and Done states.
Adds Jira comments that summarize implementation files, commits, and notes.
Connects Jira issue progress with Claude Code TodoWrite task tracking.
limitations: Requires Jira Cloud email, API token, base URL, and project key configuration.
Examples assume a team-managed Jira workflow and may need field changes.
Does not automatically verify Jira permissions, boards, or workflow schemes.
The scanned package contains only SKILL.md, although it references external scripts.

use_cases.title: Create approved Jira stories
use_cases.description: Turn a work request into a structured Jira story proposal before creating it.

use_cases.title: Track engineering task status
use_cases.description: Move Jira issues through workflow states as implementation starts and finishes.

use_cases.title: Sync implementation updates
use_cases.description: Post concise implementation notes to Jira after code work is complete.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Jira Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jira story proposal for this task. Include summary, user story, acceptance criteria, definition of done, and subtasks. Ask for approval before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Approved Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved story proposal to create a Jira issue in my configured project. Create subtasks only if they were approved.

prompt_templates.title: Transition Work Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check available Jira transitions for this issue, then move it to the requested state. Report the transition used and any blocked options.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the story, request approval, create Jira items, start work, add implementation notes, and complete the issue after verification.

output_examples.input: Create a Jira story for adding password reset emails.
output: A story proposal with a user story, acceptance criteria, and definition of done.
A clear approval question before creating the Jira issue.
Suggested subtasks for email template, API endpoint, and tests.

output_examples.output: The skill checks available transitions, selects the matching Jira transition, updates the issue, and reports the result.

output_examples.input: Finish SCRUM-101 and add implementation notes.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a Jira comment with changed files, commits, and notes, then transitions the issue to Done.

best_practices: Confirm the Jira story with the user before creating or changing issues.
Query available transitions before choosing a target workflow state.
Use least-privilege Jira tokens and validate the configured Jira tenant.
anti_patterns: Do not create Jira issues from vague requirements without user approval.
Do not assume every Jira project uses the same workflow states or fields.
Do not post sensitive file paths, commit messages, or notes without review.

faq.question: Does this skill create Jira issues automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to ask for approval before creating Jira issues.

faq.question: Which Jira version does it target?
faq.answer: The examples target Jira Cloud REST API v3.

faq.question: Can it handle custom workflows?
faq.answer: Yes, it tells the assistant to query available transitions before changing state.

faq.question: Does it include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: The scanned package contains only SKILL.md, although the documentation references scripts.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: It expects Jira email, API token, base URL, project key, and optional board ID.

faq.question: Can it sync implementation details?
faq.answer: Yes, it shows how to post files, commits, and notes to Jira comments.
